title: Groundwater: How an Aquifer Fills and Empties

segments.say: Long before tube wells, Indians built stepwells, stairs down to water hidden under the ground. That hidden water is groundwater.

anim.title: How an aquifer fills
items: It soaks into soil and rock
It fills the gaps in sand, gravel and cracked rock
That wet layer is an aquifer

segments.say: When rain soaks into the ground, it fills the tiny gaps in sand, gravel and cracked rock. A layer that holds and gives up water like this is called an aquifer.

anim.title: The water table
items: The top of the wet layer
Falls when we pump more than the rain puts back

segments.say: The top of that wet layer is the water table. It rises after the monsoon, and falls when we take out more than the rain puts back.
From the nineteen sixties, cheap pumps and tube wells changed everything. Farmers could lift water from deep below, whenever they wanted.

anim.title: How much we take out
anim.below: of the yearly refill is pumped out, across India

segments.say: Today India is the world's largest user of groundwater. Across the country, we pump out about sixty per cent of what refills each year. Most of it goes to irrigation.
But that's an average. In parts of Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan and Tamil Nadu, more is pumped than refills, and wells must go deeper every year.
For GS One: recharge fills the aquifer, extraction empties it, and the water table shows which one is winning.

sources: NCERT Class 12, India: People and Economy, ch. 6 (Water Resources): groundwater use is high in Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan and Tamil Nadu; tube wells and over-use; recharge

Central Ground Water Board, Dynamic Ground Water Resources of India 2023 and 2024: stage of groundwater extraction about 60% nationally; most extraction is for irrigation; blocks classed safe, semi-critical, critical and over-exploited
World Bank, 'Deep Wells and Prudence' (2010) and CGWB: India is the largest user of groundwater in the world
NCERT Class 7, Our Environment, ch. on water / Class 9 science: water table, infiltration and aquifers

options: A layer of rock or sand that holds and gives up water
quiz.why: Rainwater fills the gaps in sand, gravel or cracked rock: that layer is an aquifer.

quiz.q: Roughly what share of the yearly refill does India pump out, on average?
